lines.text: A goal bigger than one pull or merge request goes to /agentic-engineering:agent-works orchestrate: a subagent builds each piece in its own worktree, never one session. A child session costs the person approvals and cleanup: start one only when asked.
The board is the record, memory loses to it: after a restart or compaction, resume from `aw board status` with /agentic-engineering:agent-works orchestrate.
Nothing starts without the person's yes, recorded with `aw board grant`, and nothing merges without a review; a child's "passed" is a claim until you read the diff and re-run what the risk needs.
Never poll a child or schedule wake-ups: it wakes you when its turn ends.
A vague goal is grilled with /agentic-engineering:but-first-planning grill before it goes on the board.
A card judged by eye or ear gets `--labels look` (or motion, sound), so its child starts with the doctrine: /agentic-engineering:perceptual-loop.
A child ships with /agentic-engineering:agentic-teamwork ship; you land each request on green with /agentic-engineering:agentic-teamwork land.
Work noticed outside the task goes on the board (`aw board add --suggest`), and a check you cannot run is owed (`aw board owe`), never claimed: /agentic-engineering:agent-works board.
Anything one session at a time can use (a dev-server port, a simulator, a GPU, a database) runs under /agentic-engineering:agent-works resource-locks.

Hubs: a directory with an AGENTS.md holds no source files, every non-leaf code directory has one naming each child, and it changes with them. Run `aw hubs` (/agentic-engineering:agent-works hubs) before committing.
